Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres — Nxeon hosting platform), a real git repo. Standing rule: NEVER build/run dev servers/run `npm run build` in the live prod tree `/opt/nxeon` or the shared staging tree `/opt/nxeon-staging` — a past agent clobbering `.next` there broke production. Start by creating your own isolated worktree:
```
cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wip-registrar-phase1 -b feature/registrar-consolidation-phase1
cd /opt/nxeon-wip-registrar-phase1 && npm install
```
Do ALL reading, editing, building, and testing inside `/opt/nxeon-wip-registrar-phase1` from that point on.

CONTEXT: There is an approved implementation plan at `/root/.claude/plans/validated-napping-possum.md` for adding Namecheap and Enom as additional domain registrars alongside the existing name.com integration, so Nxeon can always source a domain from whichever registrar is cheapest after markup, while never revealing the registrar's identity to customers (admin-only visibility). Read that ENTIRE plan file first — it has the full context, the confirmed customer-facing leak audit, and the phased approach. You are implementing ONLY Phase 1 of that plan right now — the consolidation. Do NOT touch Phase 2 onward (no new `RegistrarClient` interface, no Namecheap/Enom code, no schema changes) — this task is scoped strictly to Phase 1, a pure refactor with zero behavior change, meant to ship to production on its own before any second registrar exists.

## What Phase 1 is (from the plan, restated precisely)

There are currently 3 separate hardcoded name.com HTTP clients in this codebase, not one:
1. `lib/registrar.ts` — the main one (uses a private `nc()` helper: fetch + HTTP Basic auth + `AbortSignal.timeout`).
2. `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts` — has its OWN private `nc()`/`baseUrl()`/`authHeader()` clone, used by `updateNameservers`, `setWhoisPrivacy`, `requestTransferOut` (the unlock + getAuthCode calls for outbound transfer).
3. `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts` — has ANOTHER private `nc()` clone, used for URL forwarding CRUD and registrar lock (`:lock`/`:unlock`).

Task: move every name.com HTTP call currently duplicated in files #2 and #3 into `lib/registrar.ts` as new exported functions (following that file's existing naming/style conventions exactly — look at how `registerDomain`, `renewDomain`, `listRecords`, etc. are already written there), then delete the private `nc()`/`baseUrl()`/`authHeader()` clones in files #2 and #3, updating their call sites to import and use the newly-consolidated `lib/registrar.ts` exports instead.

Concretely, functions to move into `lib/registrar.ts`:
- From `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts`: whatever `updateNameservers` needs (the `:setNameservers` call), whatever `setWhoisPrivacy` needs, and `requestTransferOut`'s `:unlock` and `:getAuthCode` calls.
- From `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts`: the URL-forwarding CRUD calls and the registrar lock (`:lock`/`:unlock`) calls.

Read every line of all three files fully before starting — you need to understand the EXACT current behavior (including SANDBOX-mode branches, error handling, and any subtle per-function differences) well enough to move it verbatim with zero behavior change, not reimplement it from scratch. This is a refactor, not a rewrite — if you find yourself changing what a function actually does (not just where it lives), stop and reconsider; the whole point of shipping this phase alone first is that it's provably behavior-identical.

`errMsg()` helpers currently duplicated in `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts` and `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts` are generic "stringify an unknown error" helpers, NOT registrar-specific — leave those alone, do not move them (the plan file notes this explicitly).

## Standing rules for this repo (non-negotiable)

- Any Prisma schema change must be written as a migration file for human review — you must NEVER run `prisma migrate deploy`/`db push` or apply one yourself. This task shouldn't need any schema change at all; if you find yourself wanting one, stop and flag it instead of proceeding.
- Never rotate, regenerate, or touch any live credential (API keys, tokens) on any real infrastructure.
- Match the codebase's existing comment style: comments explain non-obvious WHY, not WHAT. Don't over-comment.
- Zero behavior change is the entire point of this phase — do not "improve" anything beyond the consolidation itself (no refactoring the error message format, no changing SANDBOX behavior, no touching the `disableRegistrarAutorenew` logic already in `lib/registrar.ts` — leave it exactly as-is).

## Verification (required before reporting done)

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. Full test suite (`npm test`), diffed by exact failing-test-name against a fresh run on `main` in the same worktree — zero NEW failures.
3. This consolidation touches every customer-facing domain-management action (nameservers, WHOIS toggle, outbound transfer unlock/authcode, URL forwarding CRUD, registrar lock) — per the plan, this needs its own staging-equivalent smoke verification independent of anything else. Since you're in an isolated worktree without a live staging deploy, do your best with: (a) a careful line-by-line diff review confirming the moved code is byte-for-byte behavior-identical (same HTTP method, same path, same body shape, same error handling) to what it replaced, and (b) if you can spin up a local dev server against a test/sandbox registrar config (check `.env`/`NAMECOM_ENV=dev` for name.com's own real sandbox API), actually exercise a nameserver update, WHOIS toggle, and DNS forwarding call end-to-end. Be explicit in your report about what you could and couldn't verify this way.
4. Commit your work on the `feature/registrar-consolidation-phase1` branch inside the worktree (do not push, do not merge to main, do not deploy anywhere — this needs the platform owner's review before it goes anywhere near staging/production, consistent with how every other change in this session has been promoted only after explicit review).

Report back with: the exact list of functions moved (old location → new `lib/registrar.ts` export name), confirmation that the 2 duplicate `nc()`-style clients are fully deleted, confirmation of tsc/test results, what you could/couldn't verify live and how, and anything you found while reading the 3 files that doesn't match the plan's description (e.g. a 4th duplicate client, a behavior difference between the files that makes "just move it" ambiguous) — flag those clearly rather than silently picking one behavior.

1	# Multi-registrar domain sourcing (name.com + Namecheap + Enom)
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Nxeon sells domains through exactly one registrar today (name.com), via a reseller API. The owner wants to add Namecheap and Enom as additional backends so that every domain search/purchase automatically uses whichever registrar is cheapest after Nxeon's markup — maximizing margin and/or offering customers the best price — while the registrar's identity stays completely invisible to customers (search results, error messages, DNS/nameserver copy, the AI chat assistant) and visible only in admin views, per-domain.
6	
7	This scope was built from a full audit of the existing registrar code and every customer-facing surface that currently names "name.com" directly. Two structural findings shape the whole plan:
8	
9	- **There are 3 separate hardcoded name.com HTTP clients today**, not one: `lib/registrar.ts` (the main one), plus private duplicates inside `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts` (nameservers/WHOIS/outbound-transfer) and `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts` (URL forwarding/registrar lock). Designing a multi-registrar interface against 3 different existing shapes at once is how it ends up wrong in three different ways — they must be consolidated into one `NameComRegistrar` implementation FIRST, as a pure no-behavior-change refactor, before any second registrar is added.
10	- **The registrar decision must freeze at the same moment as the price it's paired with.** `purchaseDomain`'s direct-wallet path re-quotes fresh right before charging; its card path freezes `{priceCents, costCents}` into a `DomainOrderIntent` row at Stripe-session-creation time and never re-quotes at fulfillment. Once multiple registrars exist, "cheapest registrar" is part of that same frozen quote — `DomainOrderPrice`/`DomainOrderIntent` need a `registrar` field alongside `priceCents`/`costCents`, not a separate re-decision step later. Getting this wrong means a card order quoted against one registrar could silently try to fulfill through a different (by-then-cheaper) one, which has no record of that domain — invisible to the customer, but a real operational bug.
11	
12	Also found: `Domain.registrar` (`prisma/schema.prisma`) already has `@default("namecheap")` even though every write site hardcodes the literal `"name.com"` — a landmine nobody has hit yet only because every create site sets it explicitly. Fix this default as part of the schema work.
13	
14	## Confirmed customer-facing registrar-identity leaks (must be closed as part of this work)
15	
16	1. `app/dashboard/domains/page.tsx:83` — nameserver label literally "Default (name.com)".
17	2. `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:346` — a badge reading "name.com DNS".
18	3. `components/customer/DomainAdvanced.tsx:80,87` — "name.com" badge + "moves DNS off name.com's servers" copy.
19	4. `components/customer/DomainRedirects.tsx:68,72,147,219` — "live via name.com" / "name.com URL forwarding" copy (×3).
20	5. `lib/actions-domains.ts:344` — customer-facing error string says "(name.com API keys missing)".
21	6. **Biggest leak vector**: every `nc()`-style helper throws `` `name.com: ${msg}` ``, and every catch site across `lib/actions-domains*.ts` passes that raw message straight through as `{error: ...}` into customer components — so any registrar-side failure (e.g. the real "name.com: Payment failed" seen in production) is shown verbatim, registrar name included.
22	7. `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts`'s `setWhoisPrivacy()` returns a customer-facing note interpolating `` `WHOIS privacy at ${domain.registrar}...` ``.
23	8. `lib/kb-tools.ts:642` — `describeService()` feeds `` `Registrar: ${domain.registrar}` `` into the AI live-chat assistant's context, which a signed-in customer's chat could echo back.
24	
25	## Approach
26	
27	### Phase 1 — Consolidate the 3 name.com clients into one `NameComRegistrar`
28	
29	Pure refactor, zero behavior change, ships to production on its own before any second registrar exists. Move every name.com call currently duplicated in `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts` (`updateNameservers`, `setWhoisPrivacy`, `requestTransferOut`'s unlock/getAuthCode) and `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts` (URL forwarding CRUD, registrar lock) into `lib/registrar.ts` as new exported functions. Delete both files' private `nc()`/`baseUrl()`/`authHeader()` clones; both call sites import the consolidated exports instead. This collapses 3 separate `` `name.com: ${msg}` `` error-formatting sites down to 1, which Phase 5 depends on. Verify with `npm test` plus a full staging smoke pass (nameserver update, WHOIS toggle, transfer-out unlock, URL forwarding CRUD, registrar lock toggle) before touching anything else.
30	
31	### Phase 2 — The `RegistrarClient` abstraction
32	
33	New `lib/registrars/types.ts` defines the interface covering everything a registrar does today: `checkDomains`, `registerDomain`, `renewDomain`, `domainInfo`, `disableRegistrarAutorenew`, the inbound-transfer lifecycle (`checkTransfer`/`createTransfer`/`getTransfer`/`cancelTransfer`/`listTransfers`), DNS CRUD (`listRecords`/`addRecord`/`deleteRecord`/`getDnsHosts`), and the Phase-1-consolidated nameserver/WHOIS/lock/forwarding functions. Each implementation also exposes `id` ("namecom"/"namecheap"/"enom", the DB/dispatch value) and `label` ("name.com"/"Namecheap"/"eNom", admin-display-only — never passed to a customer-facing function). `transferOutcome`/`transferStatusLabel` and `domainMarkupPct`/`retailCents` stay free, registrar-agnostic functions — status bucketing and markup are platform concepts, not per-registrar behavior.
34	
35	`lib/registrars/index.ts` exports `ALL_REGISTRARS`, `configuredRegistrars()` (env-configured AND admin-enabled, see Phase 7), and `registrarById(id)`.
36	
37	**Dispatch rule**: for a domain that already has a DB row, every call site resolves `registrarById(domain.registrar)` and calls through that — critical because a domain fulfilled through Namecheap has no record at name.com, so it must never silently fail over to a different backend even if that backend later gets disabled for new business. For a new search/quote (no DB row yet) or a new inbound-transfer quote, fan out to `configuredRegistrars()` instead (Phase 3).
38	
39	### Phase 3 — Price-shopping mechanism
40	
41	`lib/tools/domain-availability.ts`'s `checkAvailabilityBatched()` (the shared cache/batch/rate-limit wrapper used by both the marketing domain checker and the signed-in wizard) becomes a fan-out: each configured registrar keeps its own cache entries (key becomes `(registrarId, domain)`, since two registrars quoting the same domain are two different facts), its own batch size (name.com's verified 24/call does not necessarily apply to Namecheap/Enom — must be verified per-registrar against real endpoints), and its own rate-limit bucket (`` `registrar:availability:${registrarId}:global` ``, so one registrar's outage/slowness can't throttle the others). 42	
43	The purchase-time re-check (`checkDomains([domain])`, currently called fresh right before charging) becomes `quoteCheapest(domain)`, fanning out to all configured registrars with no cache (this is deliberately the anti-staleness check), returning the winning `{registrar, check}`. `DomainOrderPrice`/`DomainOrderIntent` gain a `registrar` field so the card-payment path's frozen quote and the eventual `registerDomain`/`disableRegistrarAutorenew` calls agree on which backend to use.
44	
45	**Markup stays a single global percentage** (`domainMarkupPct()`, unchanged) applied uniformly to whichever registrar's cost wins — this keeps "cheapest cost," "cheapest retail," and "best margin for Nxeon" all pointing at the same registrar automatically, avoiding a three-way tradeoff. 46	
47	### Phase 4 — Real Namecheap/Enom integration work (owner action items called out plainly)
48	
49	I have not verified current 2026 account-approval terms, minimum-balance requirements, or sandbox capabilities for either registrar — these change and are gated behind an application process, so they need to be checked directly against each registrar's live reseller documentation before committing to a timeline:
